title: Console sensorization: add eviction & queue-pressure signals to prevent stealth capacity events
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Summary:
During a capacity regression on 2026-02-08 a subset of tenants experienced prolonged request tail latency and elevated 429/503 errors. The incident runbook identified autoscale capacity as healthy, but the Console dashboards did not surface the true root cause: large KV-cache eviction bursts triggered by transient memory pressure on a serving shard. Existing telemetry showed only aggregate cache hit/miss rates and a coarse ingress queue depth metric which masked per-tenant eviction storms and queue-backpressure.

Why this ticket: 
This ticket captures follow-up work from the postmortem to close observability blind spots that allowed the problem to go undetected until user-facing errors. The goal is to add fine-grained eviction, queue pressure, and trace-enrichment signals, rebuild dashboards and alerts, and validate end-to-end detection and remediation playbooks.

Scope of work (high level):
- Add new metrics: kv_cache.evictions_total (tagged by node, shard, tenant, eviction_reason), kv_cache.eviction_rate_per_min, ingress.queue_depth.(p50|p95|p99) per-tenant, and shard.memory_pressure indicators.
- Add trace attributes: span attribute kv.eviction_reason and kv.post_eviction_latency to correlate eviction events with request tails.
- Rework Console dashboards: per-tenant tail-latency + eviction heatmap, eviction correlated with queue depth, and a compact incident triage dashboard for on-call.
- Create alerts and runbook: thresholding for eviction_rate_per_min and sustained queue_depth spikes (with automatic runbook link and suggested mitigation steps).
- End-to-end validation: chaos test creating controlled eviction bursts in staging to verify detection and alert fidelity.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboards show eviction_count by tenant and eviction_reason with <=15s ingestion latency.
- Trace spans include kv.eviction_reason and can be correlated for at least 95% of eviction events within a 5-minute window.
- Alerts fire for sustained eviction_rate_per_min above defined threshold and page on-call with playbook steps.
- A short chaos runbook demonstrates that the new signals detect simulated eviction storms and that the mitigation playbook reduces tail latency.

Notes on trade-offs and constraints:
- We will emit eviction_reason tag which increases cardinality; to mitigate cost we will restrict reason values to a short enumerated set (memory_pressure, ttl_expire, size_based, explicit_delete) and redact tenant IDs into hashed buckets for aggregated dashboards. Full tenant-level tagging will be opt-in for Dedicated customers via runtime config.
- The low-latency ingestion requirement may conflict with our long-term metrics retention pipeline; initial implementation will use a high-cardinality short-term metrics hotstore (14 days) and roll aggregated summaries into long-term store.

Related artifacts:
- Postmortem notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.in/incident/2026-02-08-kv-eviction-capacity-regression
- Initial PR for metric changes (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245
- Dashboard draft (Console): https://console.redwood.in/dashboards/d/eviction-heatmap
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.in/runbooks/kv-eviction-detection

Stakeholders:
- Runtime team: implement metric emission and trace enrichment (Ravi M., Lian Zhou)
- Console team: dashboard and alert UX (Maya Flores)
- SRE/On-call: validate alerts and playbooks (Diego Alvarez)
- PM: product validation and customer communication (Priya Desai)

Risks:
- Metric cardinality blowup causing cost spike. Mitigation: enumerated reason set + hashed tenant buckets + sampling strategy for traces.
- False positives from transient eviction bursts. Mitigation: hysteresis in alerts and require sustained windows before paging.

Next steps (short term):
1) Runtime PR to add eviction metrics and trace attributes (owner: Ravi Kapoor) - target: 2026-02-17.
2) Console dashboard prototype and alert wiring (owner: Maya Flores) - target: 2026-02-24.
3) Staging chaos test and alert validation (owner: SRE) - target: 2026-03-03.
4) Post-deploy retro and doc update, ship runbook and customer advisory (owner: Priya Desai) - target: 2026-03-10.

2026-02-12 - Ravi Kapoor: Drafted runtime PR and opened initial instrumentation patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245. Need review from Lian for memory accounting code path.

2026-02-15 - Lian Zhou: Reviewed PR, added guard to only emit detailed eviction tags when config flag enabled. Suggested metric name kv_cache.evictions_total with labels: node, shard, tenant_bucket, reason.
2026-02-20 - Maya Flores: Dashboard wireframes uploaded at https://console.redwood.in/dashboards/d/eviction-heatmap. Requested a compact triage view for on-call with top-3 tenant contributors.

2026-02-25 - Diego Alvarez: SRE validated alert thresholds in staging; observed noisy alerts at low thresholds. We will add 5-minute sustained window and require 2 out of 3 shards to exceed before paging.
2026-03-02 - Priya Desai: Customer comms template drafted; recommending proactive advisory for tenants with high eviction histories and opt-in for full tenant tagging in Dedicated customers.
2026-03-02 - Ravi Kapoor: Marking runtime PR as ready for merge pending perf test results; tagging ENG-60123 as follow-up for sampling config tuning.
